brief:
Gadi Eisenkot emerged Thursday as the frontrunner to form Israel's next government after a religious party long aligned with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declined to recommend him, Al-Monitor reported. The party's decision to withhold its endorsement opens the possibility of alternative coalition arrangements centered on Eisenkot.

The shift represents a departure from the religious party's traditional backing of Netanyahu, reshaping the landscape for upcoming government-formation talks.
dek: Gadi Eisenkot emerged on Thursday as the favourite to be tasked with trying to form an Israeli government as a religious party long aligned with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declined to recommend him.
title: Religious party abandons Netanyahu as Eisenkot eyes government formation
